title: AZ-104 vs AZ-204: Azure Admin or Developer?
subtitle: Azure cloud admin or Azure cloud developer: which Microsoft Associate to target in 2026

pros: By far the most in-demand Azure cert — roughly 2.5x more job postings than the AZ-204 (LinkedIn / WTTJ France, 2026).
Senior median salary of €60k in France, €75k in Luxembourg (Hays/APEC 2026) — the best employability in the Azure Associate lineup.
The natural prerequisite for the AZ-305 (Solutions Architect Expert) — about 60% of the content reappears in more depth.
Covers identity (Entra ID), networking (VNet, NSG, peering), storage, compute and monitoring — a solid base for every Azure ops role.
cons: A very wide surface (identity, governance, networking, storage, compute, backup, monitoring) — ~150 hours to truly master it.
No application development: if you want to code on Azure (Functions, App Service, Cosmos), the AZ-204 remains essential.
The Portal case-study questions are sometimes pedantic about exact portal labels (RG, PIP, vNICs, etc.).
An ops / infrastructure exam — not a fit for developers who want to stay at the application layer.
certs.bestFor: You're targeting Cloud Administrator, Platform Engineer, Azure Cloud Ops or Azure SRE roles, or moving a sysadmin/network job onto Azure — a role where you configure and operate the platform every day.

pros: The only Microsoft Associate that validates cloud-native developer skills on Azure: App Service, Functions, Cosmos DB, Service Bus, Event Grid, Key Vault, Container Apps.
Highly valued at consultancies delivering .NET / REST APIs on Azure — often requested for senior Azure backend developer engagements.
100% multiple choice + case studies — no graded lab, so less technical stress on exam day.
Very useful for the AZ-400 (DevOps Engineer Expert): half the content (CI/CD, Functions, App Service, Key Vault) overlaps.
cons: Employer recognition about 2.5x narrower than the AZ-104 — many recruiters don't distinguish the AZ-104 from the AZ-204 and default to the former.
Median salary comparable to a senior .NET developer without the cert (~€55-60k in France) — the AZ-204 alone doesn't raise an experienced developer's salary.
Implicit prerequisite: being comfortable in C#/.NET or Node.js already — the cert doesn't teach the language.
Not the natural path to the AZ-305 (Architect Expert) — the logical next step for developers is the AZ-400 (DevOps).
certs.bestFor: You're a backend developer (.NET, Node, Python) already shipping code on Azure (App Service, Functions, Cosmos), or you want to formalize your move into cloud-native development.

verdicts.profile: You're undecided and want to maximize your interview chances.
verdicts.why: The AZ-104 shows up in 2.5x more postings and every Azure recruiter recognizes it — it is the default choice when your target role isn't locked in.

verdicts.profile: You're a .NET / Node / Python developer already shipping on Azure.
verdicts.why: The AZ-204 validates exactly your job (App Service, Functions, Cosmos, Service Bus, Key Vault). It is the only Azure Associate that proves you can write cloud-native code.

verdicts.profile: You're targeting Azure Cloud Architect or Platform Engineer roles.
verdicts.why: These roles expect the AZ-104 as a prerequisite: identity (Entra ID), networking (VNet/NSG), governance and monitoring are exactly what gets tested in architecture and consulting interviews.

verdicts.profile: You're ultimately aiming for the AZ-305 (Solutions Architect Expert).
verdicts.why: The AZ-104 is the natural prerequisite: about 60% of its content (identity, networking, governance, security) reappears in more depth on the AZ-305. The AZ-204 would point you toward the AZ-400 (DevOps Expert) instead.

verdicts.profile: You're ultimately aiming for the AZ-400 (DevOps Engineer Expert).
verdicts.why: The AZ-400 requires EITHER the AZ-104 OR the AZ-204. On the dev / CI-CD / release side, the AZ-204 → AZ-400 route is more natural: half the content (Functions, App Service, Key Vault, Pipelines) overlaps.

verdicts.profile: You want the best starting salary without a fixed target role.
verdicts.why: Senior median of ~€60k in France for the AZ-104 vs ~€55-60k for an Azure developer without a cert signal — the gap comes from the AZ-104 opening better-paid, harder-to-fill Cloud Ops / Platform / Architect roles.

verdicts.profile: You work at a consultancy or MSP delivering .NET / APIs on Azure.
verdicts.why: The AZ-204 is exactly the cert Azure consultancies ask of their backend developers: App Service, Functions, Cosmos, Service Bus, Key Vault, App Insights monitoring — their everyday stack.

verdicts.profile: You're preparing a bid or Microsoft Solutions Partner designation for your company.
verdicts.why: Microsoft Solutions Partner designations (Azure Infrastructure, Digital & App Innovation) count the AZ-104 and AZ-305 first. The AZ-204 also counts toward Digital & App Innovation, but with a narrower weighting.

verdicts.profile: You're moving from a Windows / VMware sysadmin job to Azure.
verdicts.why: The AZ-104 is built for this profile: the VMware/AD/GPO → Azure VM/Entra ID/Azure Policy transition is explicitly covered. The AZ-204 requires development fundamentals you probably don't have.

verdicts.profile: You want to pass both within 6 months.
verdicts.why: Start with the AZ-104: it gives you the platform context (identity, networking, governance) without which you'll struggle on the AZ-204 case studies. You then follow with the AZ-204 in ~80 extra hours instead of 130 from scratch.

tldr: AZ-104 if you don't know which role to target, you're aiming for Azure admin/architect/ops, or you're moving from a sysadmin job — it is the default Azure cert, better paid and more widely recognized. AZ-204 only if you're already a backend developer (.NET/Node/Python) shipping cloud-native code on Azure (App Service, Functions, Cosmos) and want to formalize that skill.
